title: Dementia: type, stage and behavior
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's cognitive disorder.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for dementia and behavioral management.

HPI
The patient is an 85-year-old male presenting for a scheduled follow-up regarding his progression of Alzheimer's disease. He is currently experiencing a severe stage of cognitive decline, which significantly impacts his activities of daily living. His daughter reports that the primary concern today is increased agitation during the evening hours. She notes that he becomes increasingly restless and difficult to soothe as the sun sets. He is currently unable to perform independent self-care and requires maximum assistance from caregivers. There have been no recent falls or acute changes in his physical health, but the behavioral symptoms are becoming more frequent.

Review of Systems
Negative for chest pain, shortness of breath, or recent fevers. Negative for weight loss or changes in appetite. Positive for behavioral agitation and cognitive impairment.

Social History
The patient lives at home with his daughter and a part-time caregiver. He is retired. He does not smoke and does not consume alcohol.

Family History
Father had hypertension. Mother had early-onset dementia.

Vitals
BP: 138/84 mmHg
HR: 72 bpm
RR: 16 breaths/min
Temp: 98.6 F
SpO2: 96% on room air

Recent Labs
HbA1c: 6.4%
eGFR: 62 mL/min
TSH: 2.1 mIU/L
Sodium: 139 mEq/L
Potassium: 4.1 mEq/L

Medication List
Donepezil 10 mg daily
Memantine 10 mg twice daily
Lisinopril 10 mg daily

Exam
The patient is alert but appears disoriented to time and place. He is able to follow simple one-step commands but struggles with complex directions. He exhibits a severe dementia profile with significant memory loss. During the exam, he appeared somewhat agitated, shifting in his chair and displaying restless movements. Skin is intact and dry. Heart sounds are regular. Lungs are clear to auscultation.

Assessment
1. Alzheimer's disease, severe stage.
2. Behavioral agitation, primarily occurring in the evening.

Plan
Continue current medications for cognitive maintenance. To address the evening agitation, I will initiate a low-dose medication trial to improve evening stability. The daughter will be instructed on non-pharmacological techniques, including a consistent bedtime routine and reducing environmental stimuli in the late afternoon. We will reassess the efficacy of the new regimen in four weeks.

Electronically signed,
P. O'Brien, PA-C
May 14, 2026
explanations: Alzheimer's disease: G30.9, sequenced first; the dementia is then coded with F02.- (dementia in other diseases classified elsewhere).
Alzheimer's disease (F02.-, dementia in other diseases), severe, with agitation: F02.C11.

distractors.why: F02.- is a manifestation code: code first the underlying Alzheimer's disease (G30.9).
The provider documents the stage (severe): it decides the code and the HCC.
Agitation is documented: use the 'with agitation' code.
Dementia due to Alzheimer's disease is F02.- (in other diseases), not F03.- (unspecified dementia).
